edges.effect_quant: The occupational solar-radiation literature consistently places outdoor work on the harmful side for basal cell carcinoma, although the exact excess risk varies with latitude, duration, and protective behavior.
edges.mechanism: Outdoor work increases cumulative solar ultraviolet exposure to skin over many years, creating a direct pathway to keratinocyte DNA damage and carcinogenesis. This is one of the clearer occupational-environmental relationships in the dermatology space because the exposure mechanism is straightforward.
edges.summary: The updated review with meta-analysis found that occupational solar exposure is associated with higher basal cell carcinoma risk, confirming the earlier systematic review. A newer nationwide cohort on occupational solar ultraviolet radiation and non-melanoma skin cancer also supports the same general harmful direction, making this a solid occupational skin-cancer edge rather than a speculative one.
edges.caveats: Risk depends on geography, lifetime sun dose, skin phenotype, and use of protective clothing or sunscreen. Some studies combine different non-melanoma skin cancer outcomes, so the exact BCC-specific magnitude remains less precise than the overall direction.
